questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a commercial occupation?
questions.explanation: A Salesperson is directly involved in selling goods and services, which defines a commercial occupation. Factory workers and engineers are classified under industrial occupations, while teachers fall under service occupations.

distractorRationale.a: a. Factory worker - This is an industrial occupation focused on production.
distractorRationale.b: b. Teacher - This is a service occupation focused on education.
distractorRationale.c: d. Engineer - This is also an industrial occupation related to manufacturing.

questions.stem: Which factor is least likely to influence a person's choice of occupation?
questions.explanation: Weather conditions typically do not affect career choices, while personal interests, economic conditions, and family expectations are significant influences on occupational decisions.

distractorRationale.a: a. Personal interests - This is a major factor in choosing an occupation.
distractorRationale.b: b. Economic conditions - The state of the economy can greatly influence job availability.
distractorRationale.c: c. Family expectations - Family influences can guide individuals towards certain careers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a service occupation?
questions.explanation: A Carpenter is primarily involved in the production of goods (furniture, structures), making it an industrial occupation, while the others provide services.

distractorRationale.a: a. Doctor - This is a service occupation focused on healthcare.
distractorRationale.b: b. Banker - This is a service occupation related to financial services.
distractorRationale.c: d. Hairdresser - This is also a service occupation providing personal grooming.
